To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DAMA signal may be interpreted as the annual modulation of an elastic or inelastic dark matter component.

the DAMA annual modulation data may be interpreted in the IDM in two ways, either in terms of elastic scattering with a light WIMP, or as the result of inelastic scattering of a heavier WIMP with a mass splitting of a few GeV.

(i) in the IDM a fraction of events can be channeled and the elastic scattering of light scalars can be consistent with the data, (ii) the IDM provides a simple framework for inelastic dark matter with a mass range between 50 GeV and 50 TeV that can explain the DAMA signal, (iii) the IDM can be consistent with WMAP and the relic density of the lightest scalar may be reduced to values as low as 0.1% of

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inelastic scattering of a ~ 50-50 TeV scalar WIMP is the most natural and compelling interpretation of the DAMA annual modulation in the context of the Inert Double Higgs Model.
the DAMA signal may be interpreted in the IDM in terms of elastic scattering of a ~ 10 Gev scalar WIMP or of inelastic scattering of a scalar WIMP with a mass between ~ 50 Gev and ~ 1 TeV.
a light iDM candidate is not only consistent with the DAMA data but also with the constraints from the direct detection experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IDM is able to accommodate the DAMA data with a very simple set of parameters.

the DAMA annual modulation may be reproduced in a model where the DM candidate is a scalar with mass MDM ~ 535 Ge-1 TeV, and that this scenario is consistent with WMAP constraints on the DM relic density.
the IDM offers a simple and natural framework for both elastic and inelastic dark-matter scattering.
